newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian panel approves SIA, Tata airline.
newsitem.headline: Indian panel approves SIA, Tata airline.

text.p: An Indian government panel has approved a $600 million proposal by Tata Industries Ltd and Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA) to set up a domestic airline, newspapers said on Tuesday.

The Foreign Investment Promotion Board, comprised of senior government officials, has approved the controversial proposal and sent it to the Cabinet Committee on Foreign Investment for a final decision, they said.
SIA and Tata Industries proposed the tie-up in February 1995.

Under the initial proposal, TATA Industries would hold a 60 percent stake and SIA would hold the remaining 40 percent. The Tata group subsequently offered to sell a 20 percent stake to the Indian public.
The proposal has been snagged in a bruising political fight, with opponents arguing that the new airline would harm India's state-owned domestic carrier, Indian Airlines.
Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim has been an outspoken critic of the proposed joint venture and more generally of foreign investment in domestic airlines.
